capture.final_message:
Use the standard representation of a coloring as a graph homomorphism \(G \to K_n\), together with the characterization of the chromatic number as the least number of colors.

The outer `Iff`s relate universally quantified propositions that are independently true, so prove all four universal statements separately and then assemble the two equivalences.

- Transport a coloring across a graph isomorphism (and its inverse) to establish invariance of `Colorable`.
- Use the characterization
  \[
  \chi(G)\le n \iff G\text{ is }n\text{-colorable}
  \]
  plus monotonicity of colorability to show
  \[
  \chi(G)=n+1 \iff G\text{ is }(n+1)\text{-colorable but not }n\text{-colorable}.
  \]
- For the surjectivity criterion, observe that a nonsurjective \(n\)-coloring can be relabeled using fewer than \(n\) colors. Conversely, if \(\chi(G)<n\), embed a coloring with fewer colors into `Fin n`; its image is not all of `Fin n`.
- Given an \(n\)-coloring and a pairwise adjacent family \(f:\iota\to V\), the composite
  \[
  \iota \xrightarrow{f} V \xrightarrow{C} \operatorname{Fin}(n)
  \]
  is injective, since adjacent vertices receive different colors. Cardinal comparison then gives `Nat.card ι ≤ n`.

The only delicate point is the `ENat` formulation: isolate the finite-successor/order conversions so that the least-color and strict-inequality arguments reduce cleanly to natural-number arithmetic.
